correctness.rationale: The normalized special-Hermite density has the uniform polynomial form (1), including cancellations at indices zero and one. A symbolically checked quartic polynomial identity proves the exact adjacent eigenvalue difference for every index. Its sign reduces the global ordering question to the two integer roots of a quadratic in index. Positivity at zero and infinity and an explicit negative integer index force both roots integral. Their discriminant gives exactly positive pronic areas, where factorization shows precisely two disjoint triple equalities and otherwise strict descent. The standalone checker independently integrates 44 levels and tests exact identities; finite checks are only corroboration. No unproved numerical or external certificate is used.

value.rationale: The theorem resolves a naturally motivated all-radius eigenvalue-index sorting question in the second non-Gaussian Hermite (polyanalytic) disk-localization problem. Its two simultaneously separated triple eigenvalue spaces occur at exactly the pronic disk areas, a structural phenomenon invisible from general diagonalization alone. In particular all initial Hermite subspaces are top spectral subspaces precisely at these areas, relevant to finite Weyl–Heisenberg/polyanalytic ensemble mode selection. The result is an infinite iff classification, not an arbitrary small numerical improvement.
